open_points.subject: Run pinning of flow activation
open_points.text: M26 requires “the flow activation under which the run started” and identifies it “by its position in the store's order”, but M19 pins only `flow_version_id` and `pinned_implementations`.
open_points.question: Which exact FlowActivation does a run pin, and where is that identity recorded so a later reactivation of the same version cannot change the authority of a draft-write?
options: Add the FlowActivation identity to Run
Derive the latest preceding activation from store order whenever needed
Treat any activation of the pinned version as equivalent
open_points.default_guess: Record the exact FlowActivation identity on the Run at creation.

open_points.subject: Mapped-node output trace
open_points.text: A15 says “A mapped node's trace is its elements' records; it has a record of its own, without `map_index`, only when it ran no element”, while A13 says the collected file-list reference is “stored in the node's NodeExecution outputs”.
open_points.question: Where are a non-empty mapped node's collected outputs and their list class recorded when there is no aggregate NodeExecution?
options: Write an aggregate NodeExecution after all elements
Store the collection only on downstream input records and run outputs
Attach the complete collection to the last element's NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: Write a separate aggregate record, although that contradicts A15.

open_points.subject: File-port value schema
open_points.text: M01 gives every port a `value_schema`, A02 requires every `value_schema` to be supported, and A04 requires file inputs to fit their ports, but K-10 says “the kernel does not inspect file content”.
open_points.question: What does a file port's `value_schema` describe, and how does the kernel decide that file bytes or a file fixture fit it without inspecting content?
options: Require one fixed schema representing opaque bytes/files
Validate only carriage, media type and size and ignore `value_schema` for file values
Validate a schema against file metadata
open_points.default_guess: Use one fixed opaque-file schema and validate only media type and size.

open_points.subject: Trial-case input completeness
open_points.text: A04 says a case is added when “its input values fit the contract version's input ports” and mentions checking “presence”, but does not say whether the input map must contain exactly every input port and no unknown ports.
open_points.question: Are missing inputs, extra inputs, and duplicate input names refused, and in what order relative to the listed per-port checks?
options: Require an exact input-port map
Allow omitted optional-looking ports when their schemas accept null
Ignore extra inputs
open_points.default_guess: Require exactly one value for every input port and refuse every extra name.

open_points.subject: Trial-case expected-output completeness
open_points.text: M06 says `expected_outputs` is “by output port” and A04 says “every output's digest equals the expected one”, but neither says whether a present `expected_outputs` map must cover every output port exactly.
open_points.question: Does a present expected-output set assert all outputs or may it assert only a subset, and how are missing or extra expected-output names handled?
options: Present means an exact map of all output ports
Allow partial expected-output assertions
Treat omitted output entries as requiring only schema-valid output
open_points.default_guess: Require an exact map of all output ports whenever `expected_outputs` is present.

open_points.subject: Flow endpoint identity and empty node IDs
open_points.text: A05 says “A flow input or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node”, while M14 only says `node_id` is unique within the version and never forbids the empty string.
open_points.question: May a real node have the empty `node_id`, and if not, where is that composition refusal ordered?
options: Forbid an empty node ID
Represent flow endpoints with a distinct endpoint kind instead of a sentinel
Allow an empty node ID and disambiguate it by context
open_points.default_guess: Forbid empty node IDs during malformed-request checks.

open_points.subject: Clock prohibition in the sandbox
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no clock” and A03 says clock entry points are replaced, but A03 also says “The list is closed for the release” and omits other observable clock sources such as `time.clock_gettime`, filesystem timestamps and resource timing APIs.
open_points.question: Are all unlisted ways of observing time forbidden, or are they permitted despite the no-clock rule?
options: Block every clock and timestamp source available in the pinned runtime
Permit APIs not in the closed trap list
Narrow the product claim to only the listed APIs
open_points.default_guess: Block every clock source and expand the release's closed list accordingly.

open_points.subject: Filesystem access by function code
open_points.text: K-02 says a function has “no filesystem beyond its input”, while A03 permits opening paths in “the exchange directory and the read-only runtime”.
open_points.question: May user code itself read arbitrary runtime files and read or write arbitrary exchange-directory paths, or are those locations accessible only to the runner?
options: User code may access both allowed trees
Only the runner may access them; user code gets decoded objects and bytes
User code may read runtime files but may access only designated exchange files
open_points.default_guess: Restrict user code to designated exchange files and the imports needed from the runtime.

open_points.subject: Invalid Python return values and output counting
open_points.text: A03 orders `resource_exhausted` before `contract_violation` and defines output count as “the canonical JSON bytes of every `value` output”, but arbitrary Python return values may be non-JSON, cyclic, have invalid keys, or otherwise have no canonical JSON representation.
open_points.question: How is output size determined for an invalid or non-serializable return, and which outcome wins when it is also extremely large?
options: Classify non-serializable output immediately as contract_violation
Use a bounded serializer and classify crossing the byte bound as resource_exhausted first
Treat serialization failure as crashed
open_points.default_guess: Use a bounded serializer; resource exhaustion wins if its bound is crossed, otherwise contract_violation.

open_points.subject: Sandbox stdout and stderr
open_points.text: A03 says every execution has bounded output, but its `output_bytes` count covers only returned values and files, while rule 6 says stdout is never kept and does not state how much may be emitted or how it is drained.
open_points.question: What happens when function code writes unbounded stdout or stderr: is it discarded through a bounded sink, counted against a limit, or allowed to block the process?
options: Discard through a nonblocking bounded sink
Count it against `output_bytes`
Close stdout and stderr so writes fail
open_points.default_guess: Drain and discard both streams through a fixed bounded mechanism and classify excess as resource_exhausted.

open_points.subject: Sandbox scratch-byte enforcement
open_points.text: A03 requires an exchange directory “bounded by `sandbox_scratch_bytes_max`” and says a scratch limit hit is `resource_exhausted`, but does not define whether the bound measures current allocation, cumulative writes, sparse-file logical size, or allocated blocks.
open_points.question: What exact quantity is limited for sandbox scratch space and at what point is a limit considered hit?
options: Maximum allocated filesystem bytes at any instant
Maximum logical sizes of files at any instant
Cumulative bytes written during the execution
open_points.default_guess: Limit the total logical size of all files present in the exchange directory at any instant.

open_points.subject: Failure detail versus no-payload trace
open_points.text: A15 says a NodeExecution “holds no value” and the trace “holds no payload”, while A03 stores an exception's type and message and A09 stores an excerpt of an error-response body; either can contain input or service payload verbatim.
open_points.question: May `failure_detail` contain business or personal payload text, and if not, what deterministic sanitization replaces it before storage?
options: Store bounded raw exception and response text
Store only fixed reason codes and exception types
Store raw text but only in a separately protected payload store
open_points.default_guess: Store fixed reason codes and exception types, not arbitrary messages or response bodies.

open_points.subject: Release-pinned sandbox dependencies
open_points.text: A20 says “one release fixes every ceiling and every dependency”, but only specifies “CPython 3.12” and requires whatever host `bubblewrap` is present, without exact patch or bubblewrap versions.
open_points.question: Which exact CPython patch release, bubblewrap version, operating-system facilities and compatibility checks define release v1 behavior?
options: Pin and verify exact versions
Declare minimum compatible versions and accept behavioral variation
Package the complete sandbox runtime with the release
open_points.default_guess: Package or verify exact CPython and bubblewrap versions for the release.

open_points.subject: Store order within a transaction
open_points.text: K-17 and A18 rely on “one order” of records, while several store calls atomically write multiple records, such as an EffectAttempt conclusion, NodeExecution, values and approval status.
open_points.question: How are distinct records written in the same transaction ordered relative to one another?
options: Assign every inserted record a monotonically increasing position in a specified field order
Give all records in one transaction the same position plus a type tie-breaker
Order only selected record types and leave others unordered
open_points.default_guess: Assign individual consecutive positions in an explicitly specified write order.

open_points.subject: Store position of mutable entities
open_points.text: A16 pages records in “reverse store order”, but bindings, approvals, grants, attempts and runs change status without the text saying whether their store position is their creation position or their latest transition.
open_points.question: Does updating an entity's status move it in list order, and which position is used by continuation tokens?
options: Creation position never changes
Every transition creates a new ordering position
Lists order by the latest transition while tokens identify the entity's creation position
open_points.default_guess: Keep an immutable creation position; status changes do not move the entity.

open_points.subject: Filtered pagination under status changes
open_points.text: A16 says a continuation starts below the last returned position so a record added meanwhile “never shifts, repeats or hides an item”, and also says a record whose status changes “leaves or enters the pages still to come”.
open_points.question: What happens when a record above the continuation cursor changes from nonmatching to matching, or a record below it changes in the opposite direction?
options: Use a snapshot of filter membership for the whole traversal
Re-evaluate each page and accept that records above the cursor can be missed
Restart pagination whenever mutable filters are used
open_points.default_guess: Use snapshot semantics for a paginated traversal.

open_points.subject: Equal spooled-file bytes
open_points.text: A18 says “Equal bytes are stored once” immediately after discussing both value bytes and spooled files, while K-10 and M22 make each spool belong to one run and remove it when that run ends.
open_points.question: Are equal spool bytes deduplicated across attempts or runs, and if so how are ownership, reference counts and deletion handled?
options: Do not deduplicate run-spool bytes
Deduplicate with durable reference counting
Deduplicate only within one run
open_points.default_guess: Do not deduplicate spool bytes; apply content deduplication only to durable values and fixtures.

open_points.subject: Admission verdict and automatic activation
open_points.text: A04 says an admitted verdict is followed “at once, in the same request” by an Activation, but does not say whether the verdict and activation are one store transaction or how a crash between them is recovered.
open_points.question: Can an admitted verdict exist without its required automatic activation after a crash, and what operation repairs that state?
options: Write verdict and activation atomically
Recover missing activations at startup
Leave it until the implementation is submitted again
open_points.default_guess: Write the verdict and any automatic activation in one transaction.

open_points.subject: Partial admission executions after interruption
open_points.text: A04 requires admission to run every case and record one TrialExecution per case, but gives no rule for a kernel crash after some TrialExecutions are recorded and before the verdict exists.
open_points.question: Are partial admission TrialExecutions retained as ordinary evidence, removed, or resumed, and does the next submission reuse any of them?
options: Retain them but rerun the whole corpus on the next submission
Atomically publish all admission executions with the verdict
Resume only the missing cases
open_points.default_guess: Retain them as observations but rerun the whole corpus and use only the new complete set for the verdict.

open_points.subject: Manifest revision access
open_points.text: M28 and A08 require reading `<manifest_location>/<service_id>.json` “at the configured `manifest_revision`”, but do not define what kind of repository or operation resolves that revision.
open_points.question: How does the kernel obtain bytes at a revision, how is the revision validated, and what happens when the working tree differs or the revision is unavailable?
options: Read from a local Git repository by immutable commit ID
Require `manifest_location` already to be a checkout of the configured revision
Use a release-provided manifest repository adapter
open_points.default_guess: Require a local Git repository and read blobs directly from an immutable commit ID.

open_points.subject: Selected instance absent from the manifest
open_points.text: A08 handles “the installation selects no instance” and an instance with no `api_base_url`, but does not explicitly state the result when the configuration names an instance that does not exist in the service record.
open_points.question: Does a nonexistent selected instance count as no selection, an invalid installation that stops startup, or a distinct proposal/send failure?
options: Count it as instance_not_selected
Refuse kernel startup
Use a distinct instance_not_found failure
open_points.default_guess: Refuse kernel startup because the configured selection is invalid.

open_points.subject: Allowed `api_base_url` forms
open_points.text: A08 accepts any absolute `http` or `https` URL with a host, while A09 concatenates its text with the operation path and derives the `host` header and TLS server name from it.
open_points.question: Are userinfo, query, fragment, non-root paths, percent escapes, Unicode hosts, IPv6 zone identifiers and trailing path segments allowed in `api_base_url`, and how are they joined and represented in `Host`?
options: Allow only scheme, host and optional port
Allow a base path but forbid userinfo, query and fragment
Allow every absolute URL and define component-preserving joining
open_points.default_guess: Allow scheme, host, optional port and an optional normalized base path; forbid userinfo, query and fragment.

open_points.subject: Loopback determination for plain HTTP
open_points.text: A09 permits plain HTTP when the `api_base_url` “host is a loopback address” but does not say whether this means a literal IP, a hostname that resolves to loopback, or every resolved address.
open_points.question: How is loopback status determined, especially for `localhost`, IPv6 forms and hostnames with changing or mixed DNS results?
options: Only literal loopback IP addresses qualify
Resolve once and require every result to be loopback
Treat `localhost` plus literal loopback addresses as loopback
open_points.default_guess: Only literal IPv4 or IPv6 loopback addresses qualify.

open_points.subject: HTTP header value encoding
open_points.text: A09 sends required-header values “verbatim”, while A08 and A17 allow UTF-8 text other than empty, whitespace-edged or control-containing values and do not restrict it to an HTTP wire encoding.
open_points.question: Which characters are legal in required and credential header values, and how are non-ASCII values encoded on the wire?
options: Require visible ASCII only
Allow RFC-compatible raw bytes derived from a specified encoding
Encode Unicode using a defined convention
open_points.default_guess: Require visible ASCII plus permitted horizontal spaces, with no non-ASCII characters.

open_points.subject: Meaning of control character
open_points.text: A08 and A17 refuse header or credential values that “hold a control character” without defining the character set or Unicode categories covered.
open_points.question: Does `control character` mean ASCII C0 and DEL, C1 controls too, or every Unicode character in category `Cc`?
options: ASCII C0 plus DEL
Unicode category Cc
ASCII C0, DEL and C1
open_points.default_guess: Refuse every Unicode `Cc` character, including C0, DEL-equivalent controls and C1.

open_points.subject: Multipart serialization
open_points.text: A09 specifies multipart parts and headers but does not specify boundary generation, CRLF placement, final delimiter, header quoting or escaping, while also requiring exactly one HTTP request whose request digest can be previewed.
open_points.question: What exact multipart byte serialization must every implementation produce?
options: Define a deterministic boundary and complete byte grammar
Use the HTTP library's multipart encoder
Permit any RFC-conforming serialization
open_points.default_guess: Define a deterministic boundary derived from the request inputs and a complete CRLF-based serialization.

open_points.subject: Port names in multipart headers
open_points.text: A02 permits arbitrary bounded port names, while A09 places a port name directly inside `name="<port>"` and `filename="<port>"` without an allowed-character rule or escaping rule.
open_points.question: Which port names are permitted in multipart bindings, or how are quotes, backslashes, CR/LF and non-ASCII characters escaped?
options: Restrict port names to plain field names
Apply a specified quoted-string and filename encoding
Refuse unsafe names only when proposing a multipart binding
open_points.default_guess: Require multipart binding port names to be plain ASCII field names.

open_points.subject: Approval coverage of multipart boundary
open_points.text: State 0 says an approval covers the “fully built request” and “Any difference at send ... asks again”, with only the credential value exempted, while A10 omits the multipart boundary from the request description and says “equal parts give equal descriptions”.
open_points.question: Does changing the actual multipart boundary void an approval?
options: Yes; include the exact boundary and wire body in the digest
No; multipart boundary differences are explicitly equivalent
Use a deterministic boundary so no difference can occur
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic boundary and include the resulting content type and body identity in the approved request.

open_points.subject: Media-type identity and comparison
open_points.text: K-06 requires file ports to have “the same media type”, while A09 compares response `Content-Type` “on type and subtype without regard to case and ignoring parameters”; no syntax or canonical form for a declared port media type is given.
open_points.question: May declared media types contain parameters or mixed case, and are edge equality, stored identity and HTTP response matching textual or normalized comparisons?
options: Require lowercase type/subtype with no parameters
Store original text but compare normalized type/subtype
Permit parameters and include them in edge equality but not response matching
open_points.default_guess: Require a lowercase RFC media type consisting only of type/subtype and no parameters.

open_points.subject: Data-directory privacy check
open_points.text: A18 says the data directory and everything in it are “private to the kernel's user” and the kernel refuses to start otherwise, without defining accepted owners, permission bits, ACLs or hard links.
open_points.question: What exact filesystem ownership and permission conditions pass the startup check for directories and files?
options: Owner must be the kernel user and no group/other permission bits may be set
Allow owner-only ACLs regardless of mode bits
Check only the top-level directory
open_points.default_guess: Require every directory and file to be owned by the kernel user with no group or other permissions, and reject unexpected ACL access.
